applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Double taxation agreement between Luxembourg and France, as amended

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners, as amended; CSSF Regulation 12-02; and applicable EU AML Directives as transposed into Luxembourg law.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or national identity document of each UBO and manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent authority in country of origin (civil registry or migration authority)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for HCCH 1961 member states; otherwise consular legalization by a Luxembourg embassy or consulate; plus certified French/German translation where required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing or commercial register excerpt for any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official trade/commercial register of the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization; certified translation into French, German, or English

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Evidence of residential address (recent utility bill or bank statement) for each UBO and manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or credit institution in country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original or certified true copy; notarized if non-Latin script; notarized translation into French/German where required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Criminal record extract (extrait de casier judiciaire) for proposed managers
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Justice or judicial police authority of country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization; certified translation into French or German

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All UBOs, directors and managers must be screened, before any filing, against the EU consolidated restrictive measures list (implementing UN Security Council sanctions), the Luxembourg Ministry of Finance financial sanctions list, OFAC SDN and sectoral sanctions lists, and the FATF/PEP definitions implemented under EU AML Directives. Enhanced due diligence must include source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification for PEPs, family members and high-risk third-country exposures; AML/KYC records must be retained for at least five years after the end of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Societes (RCS), lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must use the Latin alphabet; names derived from non-Latin scripts must be transliterated. The name must not be contrary to public order, must not mislead as to the statutory activity, and must include the suffix 'SARL'. All statutory and registration filings are prepared in French or German; translation of the chosen name into Luxembourgish, French, or German may be required to avoid conflict with an existing registration.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation may be renewed once for an additional 30 days before expiry. In case of rejection, the applicant must file a written request for reconsideration with the RCS/LBR within one month, attaching the rejection letter and any ministerial authorisation obtained for sensitive tokens. If the reconsideration is unsuccessful, an annulment appeal may be lodged with the Administrative Tribunal (Tribunal administratif) in Luxembourg within three months of the refusal notice.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Pure virtual mailbox arrangements are not sufficient for a Luxembourg SARL. The registered office must be a physical location in Luxembourg, accessible to RCS, tax and AML authorities. A serviced or virtual office is acceptable for the non-licensed AdTech/SSP business only if the provider maintains a substantive local physical seat, mail handling, and meeting facilities, and if the entity can demonstrate day-to-day substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 15% estimated likelihood of an unannounced physical on-site inspection within the first three years for a low-risk non-licensed AdTech platform, primarily from tax, social security and AML authorities.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg law firm / AML compliance provider

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg amended law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as consolidated; Articles 710-1 to 710-24 (Société à Responsabilité Limitée)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCSL)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Articles of Incorporation (Statuts) with accompanying RCSL registration form
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum legal capital EUR 12,000 (approx. USD 13,000); at least 25% (EUR 3,000) must be paid up on subscription and deposited in a blocked bank account at a Luxembourg credit institution
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the company is hereby incorporated in accordance with the submitted Articles of Incorporation. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the entire share capital of EUR 12,000 is duly subscribed and the statutory minimum portion of EUR 3,000 is paid up in cash, with proof of such payment delivered to the notary. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office is fixed at [Location], Luxembourg and that the Articles of Incorporation are adopted in their final form. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name] is appointed as sole manager (gérant) with full and unfettered authority to represent the company, open bank accounts, and execute all registration filings. RESOLVED, that this resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCSL online portal (eJustice.lu / brr.lu)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request through the LBR online filing interface, specifying the desired company name and proposed activity description. Attach a valid certificate of non-conformity with hotel names if applicable. Await the issuance of a reservation certificate with a 2-month validity.
required_dossiers: Identity document of the natural person seeking reservation
Proof of address of the applicant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, modify the proposed name and re-apply; if the reservation expires, renew via the same portal before formal filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening a Blocked Capital Account and Capital Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: One of the Luxembourg credit institutions or banks authorized to hold escrow accounts (e.g., BIL, BGL BNP Paribas, Société Générale Luxembourg)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct the appointed notary and bank to open a temporary blocked account in the name of the company in formation. Transfer the paid-up minimum of EUR 3,000 (or more if elected) from the shareholders' accounts. Obtain a certificate of blockage (attestation de blocage) confirming the deposit and availability of the funds for the company's benefit.
required_dossiers: Identification of all subscribing shareholders (certified copies)
Beneficial ownership declaration (behind the name of the company in formation)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the deposit certificate is delayed, provide supplementary client identification documentation and request an urgency certificate from the bank; coordinate with the notary to fast-track.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public registered with the Luxembourg Chamber of Notaries (Chambre des Notaires du Grand-Duché de Luxembourg)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation (Statuts) containing the corporate name, registered office, corporate purpose (ISIC 7310 – programmatic advertising exchange), share capital, share distribution, directors' powers, and governance rules. Convene the constitutive general meeting before a notary; all subscribers must appear either physically or by proxy. Have the notary certify the execution, verify the capital deposit certificate, and record the deed.
required_dossiers: Identification and residential addresses of shareholders
Business plan for programmatic ad exchange activities
Power of attorney if shareholders are represented
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises deficiencies in the draft, correct the articles immediately and resubmit; if a shareholder fails to appear, obtain a valid notarized power of attorney and re-schedule.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Instrument with the RCSL
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (via eJustice.lu platform or physical submission to the LBR office in Luxembourg City)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized instrument and corresponding registration application (form C – RCSL) within one month of the notarial deed. Submit electronically through eJustice.lu using an authenticated legal agent account, or physically at the RCSL counter. Pay the registration fee and obtain an RCSL business number (Numéro d'immatriculation).
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation (original or certified copy)
Acceptance of appointment by the manager (if applicable)
Identity and signature specimen of the manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is queried or rejected, cure the technical defect (e.g., missing signature page or inaccurate data) within the 15-day cure period and re-submit; request an administrative review through LBR if rejection persists.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Registration (Social Security, Tax and Trade Register)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS); Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Luxembourg Business Registers for trade register updates
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon obtaining the RCSL number, the company must register with the CCSS for employer social security coverage, with the AEDT for corporate income tax, VAT and business licensing, and with the LBR to update the list of authorised signatories and any additional substantive registrations. Obtain a business license (autorisation d'établissement) if commercial activity is performed by a manager/employee who is not an EU national or if the activity requires endorsement.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement or ownership deed for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEDT or CCSS rejects the registration due to missing data, supplement the file from the RCSL certificate and resubmit; if a business license application is refused, file an appeal to the Ministry of the Economy within one month.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy (Ministère de l'Économie) – Industry Department (no specific industrial permit because the activity is administrative and purely digital)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required – No specific operational manufacturing or industrial permit for ISIC 7310 (advertising and programmatic ad exchange) under Luxembourg law

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Environmental Protection Agency of Luxembourg)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – No formal EIA required for a non-industrial office-based ad-tech platform; if office space exceeds 1,000 m², submission of a simple architectural/energy notice may be necessary
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable; office activities fall below thresholds for wastewater discharge, VOC emissions, or hazardous waste. However, the company must comply with general waste segregation and electronics recycling rules under Luxembourg waste law (Regulation EU 2019/1021 and domestic Waste Act).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety and building safety: Obtain a certificate of conformity from the Commune (local municipal fire and building authority) for the registered office if the lease agreement requires compliance. Perform a structural load inspection only if the office premises are located in a listed historical building; otherwise attach the lease attestation. Occupational health clearance: register under the mandatory occupational medical surveillance framework (Association d'Assurance Accident – AAA) and obtain an employee workstation compliance statement from STM (Inspection du Travail et des Mines) for any workstation in an office context.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) / Luxembourg Inland Revenue; registration portal: MyGuichet.lu and the Registre national des sociétés et associations (RCSL); indirect tax authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AED) with VAT registration via MyGuichet.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity establishing a Luxembourg SARL must incorporate via a notary public and register with the RCSL (Luxembourg Business Registers). Following incorporation, the entity must file a request for a Luxembourg VAT number (numéro de TVA) with the AED, and obtain a corporate tax ID assigned by the ACD upon filing the first tax return or through the provisional registration process. Non-resident companies with no permanent establishment but with Luxembourg-source income must register directly with the ACD for a Luxembourg tax reference number and may be required to appoint a fiscal representative for VAT compliance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not maintain a check-the-box regime. A SARL is per se subject to corporate income tax (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) at entity level, plus municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal) and the solidarity surcharge. Eligible groups may elect for fiscal unity (régime d'intégration fiscale) under Article 164bis LIR for resident companies, subject to a 95% direct or indirect participation and a five-year commitment. Hybrid mismatch rules under ATAD (Article 168ter LIR) apply and may be disallowed for payments involving hybrid instruments or hybrid entities.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée - TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general VAT registration threshold for Luxembourg-established suppliers; any person carrying out taxable transactions in Luxembourg must register. Non-established businesses supplying distance sales to Luxembourg consumers are subject to the EU One-Stop-Shop (OSS) scheme once intra-Community distance sales exceed EUR 10,000 annually across the EU. An EU-established supplier exceeding EUR 100,000 of intra-Community supplies must register in Luxembourg or use the OSS for non-Union B2C electronic services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not currently mandate a nationwide real-time continuous transaction controls (CTC) clearance or clearance stamping regime for standard B2B domestic invoicing. Electronic invoicing is permitted under general VAT rules subject to authenticity, integrity and legibility; Peppol BIS Billing is the standard used for public procurement through the eFiling platform. Businesses must file periodic VAT returns electronically, and e-invoice data must be retained for the statutory ten-year period.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods to non-EU destinations may be zero-rated provided proof of export is evidenced (actual departure from the EU within 90 days for transport documentation, or within the time limits of the fiscal receipt). Advertising, DSP and SSP services supplied to non-established business customers are generally taxable at the Luxembourg place of supply (B2B general rule) and therefore not automatically zero-rated unless the customer belongs outside the EU and the service falls under Article 17(2) or 17(3) LTA (e.g., advertising services). For B2B services, Luxembourg VAT applies where the customer is established; consequently cross-border ad-tech services exported to non-EU clients are generally outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT. Services physically performed or electronically supplied to non-EU private consumers may be zero-rated or outside scope under the place-of-supply rules, subject to supporting business evidence.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Electronic Export Accompanying Document - EAD)
Transport Documents evidencing departure (CMR, Bill of Lading, Air Waybill)
Proof of Payment / Bank Transfer Records
Inward Remittance Certificate (where FDI approval triggered) or bank inward remittance advice for non-EU settlement
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Erroneous or fraudulent zero-rating claims may result in reassessment of VAT plus default interest at 0.8% per month. Intentional VAT evasion triggers criminal tax penalties of up to double the evaded tax and potentially imprisonment. Administratively, the AED can impose fines up to the amount of tax evaded and may revoke the right to apply the zero rate; directors may be held jointly liable. For goods, failure to satisfy export documentation within prescribed deadlines triggers reverse charge VAT at 17% plus penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), the national central bank of the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg and the Eurosystem member for Luxembourg; operates TARGET2-LU settlement and holds the statutory balance-of-payments statistics mandate. Prudential supervision and AML/KYC enforcement over credit institutions is shared with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF), the financial-sector regulator.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Eurozone membership and Articles 63-66 TFEU guarantee unrestricted current-account and capital-account convertibility. Luxembourg imposes no exchange-control licensing, no retention quotas, no minimum-holding periods, and no ordering or prioritisation of remittances; the EUR/USD and EUR/GBP markets are fully deliverable without any BCL involvement. Profit-remittance gates are non-regulatory and are driven by corporate law and tax law: (i) the S.à r.l. minimum share capital of EUR 12,000 must remain intact, and distributions must not reduce net assets below the share capital plus non-distributable reserves; (ii) a solvency / balance-sheet test applies to each distribution; (iii) the standard 15% Luxembourg dividend withholding tax applies to outbound profit distributions, reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive for qualifying EU corporate shareholders and to reduced treaty rates (e.g., 5% or 0% under the Luxembourg-US DTT) for non-EU investors; and (iv) intra-group interest and royalty flows must satisfy arm's-length transfer-pricing rules to preserve deductibility. No prior central-bank approval is required for any currency conversion or for the repatriation of profits, dividends, loans, or service fees.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg statutory law and BCL regulation impose no export-proceeds surrender obligation, no mandatory conversion ratio into EUR, and no statutory repatriation deadline for service receipts. A Luxembourg S.à r.l. earning USD from US programmatic ad networks, DSPs, and publishers may retain USD indefinitely in foreign-currency accounts without penalty. The only attached compliance duties are: (1) mandatory BCL balance-of-payments statistical reporting, which the bank executes automatically on the basis of the BOP purpose code stated on each cross-border payment instruction; (2) the EUR 10,000 physical-cash declaration threshold under Regulation (EU) 2018/1672; and (3) originator and beneficiary travel-rule data transmission under Regulation (EU) 2015/847 for all wire transfers. Neither the BCL nor the CSSF requires hedging, conversion, or surrender of proceeds on any timeline.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital escrow account for the statutory EUR 12,000 paid-in capital and operational EUR current account with multi-currency sub-accounts
Operational multi-currency account (EUR, USD, GBP) with SWIFT corporate e-banking, SEPA XML batch payment file capability, and cash-pooling / virtual-account overlay for publisher disbursements
Operational current account (EUR/USD) with optional virtual-IBAN segmentation for sub-ledger reconciliation of high-velocity AdTech flows
Operational EUR current account with strong digital onboarding; narrower product set for high-volume USD ACH/wire disbursements

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts filing with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS), comprising the balance sheet, profit and loss account, annex, and managers' report where applicable.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), with automatic publication in the RESA electronic gazette.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholder approval of annual accounts within six months after financial year-end; filing with RCS within one month after approval and in any event within seven months after financial year-end. For a calendar-year SARL: approval by 30 June and RCS filing by 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing is subject to a formal RCS notice, coercive daily fines imposed by the competent District Court, and criminal fines on defaulting managers; persistent non-filing for consecutive years after final formal notice may trigger administrative strike-off from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial ownership confirmation filed with the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), confirming that the disclosed UBOs and ownership percentages remain accurate.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within one month after approval of the annual accounts or, if annual accounts are not approved, within one month after the statutory deadline for approval; for a calendar-year SARL, due by 31 July following the financial year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or maintain accurate UBO data exposes the SARL and its managers to criminal fines of EUR 500 to EUR 5,000 and imprisonment of eight days to one year; repeated non-compliance may also lead to RCS strike-off and AML enforcement measures.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit is required where the SARL exceeds at least two of three thresholds for two consecutive financial years: balance sheet total above EUR 4.4 million; net turnover above EUR 8.8 million; average workforce above 50 employees. Audit is also mandatory for public-interest entities, issuers of listed securities, and group companies required to produce consolidated accounts.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Annual accounts must be prepared under Luxembourg GAAP as codified by the Law of 19 December 2002 and applicable Luxembourg professional standards transposing EU Accounting Directive 2013/34/EU. IFRS may be used where expressly permitted and is generally required for consolidated accounts of listed groups.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Any share transfer affecting direct or indirect ownership or control must be recorded in the members register and filed as an RBE amendment within thirty days of the change, regardless of the annual cycle. The annual RBE confirmation, due within one month after approval of the annual accounts, validates that the recorded UBO information remains accurate and reflects all completed share transfers.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,500 – USD 3,500 per year for a Luxembourg registered office, domiciliation service and standard company secretarial support.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 – USD 25,000 per year for a mandatory statutory audit of a comparable Luxembourg SARL; no audit fee applies if the SARL remains below the statutory audit exemption thresholds.

stage_6.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire 100 / eCDF (electronic tax declaration) via MyGuichet
stage_6.reporting_frequency: Annual; calendar-year based unless a derogatory fiscal year has been approved
stage_6.statutory_deadline_rule: By 31 December of the year following the relevant fiscal year-end (FY Y return due 31 December Y+1); quarterly advance instalments paid on 10 March, 10 June, 10 September and 10 December
